## Recommendation

```{r recommendation}
validation_rmse <- sapply(names(selected), function(m) rmse(val, m))
eligible <- names(validation_rmse)[validation_rmse <= min(validation_rmse) * 1.01]
simplicity <- c("ETS", "SARIMA", "TSLM", "DynamicRegression", "XGBoost", "LSTM")
round(sort(validation_rmse), 2)
c(Recommended = recommended, RuleCheck = simplicity[simplicity %in% eligible][1])

```

## Why the validation and test rankings differ

The recommendation follows the validation rule, but the test-period ranking is different. Three checks: the two periods have very different price levels; on the highest-price test days every model under-predicts; and the test-best model's advantage over the recommended model is not driven by a few days only. Table 12 adds a fourth: XGBoost's external variables help on validation but not on test.

```{r ranking-shift}
# Price level and volatility in the two evaluation periods
regime <- data.frame(Sample = c("Validation 2025", "Test 2026"), N = c(nrow(val), nrow(test)),
                     Mean = c(mean(val$Actual), mean(test$Actual)), SD = c(sd(val$Actual), sd(test$Actual)))
kable(regime, digits = 1, caption = "Daily USEP in the validation and test periods (SGD/MWh)")

# Mean error (actual - forecast; positive = under-prediction); high-price days = top 10% of test actuals
high <- test$Actual > quantile(test$Actual, 0.9)
bias_table <- bind_rows(lapply(top3, function(m)
  data.frame(Model = m, MeanError_val = mean(val$Actual - val[[m]]), MeanError_test = mean(test$Actual - test[[m]]),
             MeanError_test_high = mean((test$Actual - test[[m]])[high]))))
kable(bias_table, digits = 2, caption = "Mean forecast error of the three best models by test RMSE")

# How concentrated is the test-best model's advantage over the recommended model?
test_best <- top4[1]
d <- (test$Actual - test[[recommended]])^2 - (test$Actual - test[[test_best]])^2  # > 0: test-best model better that day
top10 <- order(abs(d), decreasing = TRUE)[1:10]
concentration <- data.frame(Comparison = paste(test_best, "vs", recommended),
                            ShareFromTop10Days = sum(d[top10]) / sum(d),
                            RMSE_TestBest_excl_top10 = sqrt(mean((test$Actual - test[[test_best]])[-top10]^2)),
                            RMSE_Recommended_excl_top10 = sqrt(mean((test$Actual - test[[recommended]])[-top10]^2)),
                            TestDaysNeededFor5pctDM = (qnorm(0.975) * sd(d) / mean(d))^2)
kable(concentration, digits = 2, caption = "Concentration of the test-best model's advantage")
```

# Forecasts beyond the sample: September 2026

Two layers of forecast for the month after the data end, both made with the frozen settings and data up to 31 August 2026: a one-day forecast for 1 September from every model, and a 30-day path for the whole month from SARIMA. No September value is read, so neither layer is scored.

## Next-day forecast: 1 September 2026

Forecasts for the first day after the data end, made with the frozen settings and data up to 31 August 2026. No September value is read, so these forecasts are not scored. Naive is the price of 31 August 2026.

The 80 % and 95 % intervals follow the rule of the *Prediction intervals* section: the radius is the finite-sample quantile, rank ⌈(n + 1)(1 − α)⌉, of the latest (at most 180, at least 100) one-step absolute errors realised up to 31 August 2026, applied symmetrically around the point forecast.

```{r next-day}
# the realised errors end on the last day of data, and the cached forecasts are for the day after
stopifnot(max(test$Date) == end_date, all(next_prediction$Date == end_date + 1L))

# Naive benchmark: the last observed price (2026-08-31)
next_day <- rbind(data.frame(Date = end_date + 1L, Model = "Naive", Prediction = yesterday(end_date + 1L)),
                  next_prediction[c("Date", "Model", "Prediction")])

# Interval radius: same rule as in the intervals chunk, with every validation and test error now realised
next_radius <- function(kind, alpha) {
  calibration <- tail(abs(c(val[[kind]] - val$Actual, test[[kind]] - test$Actual)), 180L)
  stopifnot(length(calibration) >= 100L)
  rank <- min(length(calibration), ceiling((length(calibration) + 1L) * (1 - alpha)))
  sort(calibration)[rank]
}
radius_80 <- vapply(next_day$Model, next_radius, numeric(1), alpha = 0.20, USE.NAMES = FALSE)
radius_95 <- vapply(next_day$Model, next_radius, numeric(1), alpha = 0.05, USE.NAMES = FALSE)
next_day$Lower80 <- next_day$Prediction - radius_80
next_day$Upper80 <- next_day$Prediction + radius_80
next_day$Lower95 <- next_day$Prediction - radius_95
next_day$Upper95 <- next_day$Prediction + radius_95
next_day <- next_day[order(-next_day$Prediction), ]
kable(next_day, digits = 2, row.names = FALSE,
      caption = "Table 15. One-day-ahead forecasts for 2026-09-01 with 80% and 95% empirical intervals (SGD/MWh)")
```

## Month-ahead forecast: September 2026

A 30-day path for 1–30 September and a forecast of the September average price, from SARIMA, the main model of this section. The frozen SARIMA specification (`selected$SARIMA$config`) is neither re-selected nor re-tuned. Only its parameters are re-estimated, on all daily prices from 1 January 2021 to 31 August 2026, with the same call as a weekly re-estimation in `rolling_predict()`. The intervals are empirical and come from the errors of a 30-day backtest. ETS, the other price-history model, appears in that backtest only. This section runs in both modes and needs neither `xgboost` nor `keras3`.

**Why 30 days.** The course brief asks for a "forecast for the next year or relevant horizon". Electricity retailers and large consumers arrange purchases and hedges month by month, so one month is the relevant horizon. And the backtest below shows that errors and intervals grow with the horizon, so a longer path would carry little information.

**Why XGBoost has no path.** XGBoost, the recommended one-day model, is shown for 1 September only and is not iterated forward. Its inputs are the previous day's demand forecast, reserve and regulation prices, fuel price and temperature, so a forecast for 2 September onwards would first need assumed or forecast values of those variables.

```{r month-ahead}
horizon <- 30L
bands <- list("Days 1-7" = 1:7, "Days 8-14" = 8:14, "Days 15-30" = 15:30)
band_of <- function(step) names(bands)[findInterval(step, vapply(bands, min, numeric(1)))]

# 30-day forecast of `kind` from the price series y, with the model's own 80% and 95% intervals. Naive and
# SeasonalNaive are the benchmarks; SARIMA and ETS keep their frozen specification and re-estimate its parameters
# on y, with the same calls as the weekly re-estimation in rolling_predict()
forecast_30 <- function(kind, y) {
  series <- ts(y, frequency = 7)
  if (kind == "Naive") return(naive(series, h = horizon, level = c(80, 95)))
  if (kind == "SeasonalNaive") return(snaive(series, h = horizon, level = c(80, 95)))
  config <- selected[[kind]]$config
  if (kind == "ETS") model <- ets(series, model = config$model, damped = config$damped)
  if (kind == "SARIMA") model <- Arima(series, order = config$order, seasonal = config$seasonal, include.constant = config$constant)
  if (kind == "ETS") set.seed(2026)  # forecast.ets() simulates the intervals of some ETS models
  forecast(model, h = horizon, level = c(80, 95))
}

# One row per forecast day: point forecast and the bounds of the model's own intervals
path_table <- function(fc, kind, dates) {
  data.frame(Date = dates, Step = seq_along(dates), Model = kind, Prediction = as.numeric(fc$mean),
             Lower80 = as.numeric(fc$lower[, "80%"]), Upper80 = as.numeric(fc$upper[, "80%"]),
             Lower95 = as.numeric(fc$lower[, "95%"]), Upper95 = as.numeric(fc$upper[, "95%"]))
}

# Fitting series: every day from 2021-01-01 to the last day of data
price_history <- daily[daily$Date <= end_date, c("Date", "DailyUSEP")]
stopifnot(min(price_history$Date) == start_date, max(price_history$Date) == end_date, !anyNA(price_history$DailyUSEP))
september_dates <- end_date + seq_len(horizon)  # 2026-09-01 to 2026-09-30

september_fc <- forecast_30("SARIMA", price_history$DailyUSEP)
september_fc$model  # frozen specification with the re-estimated parameters
```

### 30-day backtest

How well do 30-day paths of this kind forecast? The exercise is repeated inside the 2025 validation period and inside the 2026 test period. A path starts on every 7th day from 1 January (the weekly re-estimation days of the rolling forecasts) and is kept only if all 30 days lie inside the period. For each path the frozen SARIMA and ETS specifications are re-estimated on all data before its first day and forecast 30 days. `naive()` (the last price) and `snaive()` (the same weekday of the last week) forecasts from the same data are the benchmarks. The backtest has three uses: it compares the models with the benchmarks, it decides between SARIMA and ETS, and its errors give the intervals of the September forecast.

Empirical intervals follow the rule of the one-day intervals: the radius is the absolute error of rank ⌈(n + 1)(1 − α)⌉, applied symmetrically around the point forecast. The errors are pooled by band of forecast days (1–7, 8–14, 15–30), and for the 30-day average price there is one error per path. As a calibration check, the radius is taken from the 2025 errors and its coverage is counted on the 2026 paths. The September intervals themselves use the 2026 errors only.

```{r horizon-backtest}
backtest_models <- c("Naive", "SeasonalNaive", "SARIMA", "ETS")

# First days of the 30-day paths: every 7th day of the period, kept only if the whole path lies inside it
backtest_origins <- function(dates) {
  origins <- dates[seq(1L, length(dates), by = 7L)]
  origins[origins + horizon - 1L <= max(dates)]
}

run_backtest <- function(period, dates) bind_rows(lapply(backtest_origins(dates), function(origin) {
  y <- daily$DailyUSEP[daily$Date < origin]  # every price before the first forecast day, nothing later
  target <- origin + seq_len(horizon) - 1L
  bind_rows(lapply(backtest_models, function(kind)
    cbind(Period = period, Origin = origin, path_table(forecast_30(kind, y), kind, target),
          Actual = daily$DailyUSEP[match(target, daily$Date)])))
}))
backtest <- bind_rows(run_backtest("Validation 2025", validation_dates), run_backtest("Test 2026", test_dates))
stopifnot(!anyNA(backtest), max(backtest$Date[backtest$Period == "Validation 2025"]) <= validation_end, max(backtest$Date) <= end_date)
backtest$Band <- band_of(backtest$Step)

# 30-day average price: one actual and one forecast per path (no model interval is available for the average)
path_means <- backtest |>
  group_by(Period, Origin, Model) |>
  summarise(Actual = mean(Actual), Prediction = mean(Prediction), .groups = "drop") |>
  mutate(Lower80 = NA_real_, Upper80 = NA_real_, Lower95 = NA_real_, Upper95 = NA_real_)

# Accuracy, mean error (actual - forecast; positive = under-prediction) and coverage of the model's own intervals
accuracy_rows <- function(data, group) {
  data |>
    group_by(Period, Model) |>
    summarise(Horizon = group, Paths = n_distinct(Origin), N = n(),
              RMSE = sqrt(mean((Actual - Prediction)^2)), MAE = mean(abs(Actual - Prediction)),
              MeanError = mean(Actual - Prediction),
              ModelCoverage80 = mean(Actual >= Lower80 & Actual <= Upper80),
              ModelCoverage95 = mean(Actual >= Lower95 & Actual <= Upper95), .groups = "drop")
}
horizon_groups <- c(list("Day 1" = 1L, "Day 7" = 7L, "Day 14" = 14L, "Day 30" = 30L), bands)
horizon_backtest <- bind_rows(
  bind_rows(lapply(names(horizon_groups), function(group) accuracy_rows(filter(backtest, Step %in% horizon_groups[[group]]), group))),
  accuracy_rows(path_means, "30-day mean")) |>
  group_by(Period, Horizon) |>
  mutate(RMSE_gain_vs_Naive  = 1 - RMSE / RMSE[Model == "Naive"],
         RMSE_gain_vs_SNaive = 1 - RMSE / RMSE[Model == "SeasonalNaive"]) |>
  ungroup()

# Empirical interval radius: the rank rule of the one-day intervals, on all errors of a group
error_radius <- function(errors, alpha) {
  errors <- sort(abs(errors))
  errors[min(length(errors), ceiling((length(errors) + 1L) * (1 - alpha)))]
}
# Errors behind the intervals: every forecast day in its band, and one error per path for the 30-day average
interval_groups <- c(names(bands), "30-day mean")
interval_errors <- bind_rows(transmute(backtest, Period, Model, Group = Band, Error = Actual - Prediction),
                             transmute(path_means, Period, Model, Group = "30-day mean", Error = Actual - Prediction))
group_errors <- function(kind, group, periods) {
  interval_errors$Error[interval_errors$Model == kind & interval_errors$Group == group & interval_errors$Period %in% periods]
}

# Calibration check: radius from the 2025 errors, coverage counted on the 2026 paths
calibration <- bind_rows(lapply(backtest_models, function(kind) bind_rows(lapply(interval_groups, function(group) {
  radius <- c(error_radius(group_errors(kind, group, "Validation 2025"), 0.20),
              error_radius(group_errors(kind, group, "Validation 2025"), 0.05))
  test_errors <- abs(group_errors(kind, group, "Test 2026"))
  data.frame(Period = "Test 2026", Horizon = group, Model = kind,
             EmpiricalRadius80 = radius[1], EmpiricalRadius95 = radius[2],
             EmpiricalCoverage80 = mean(test_errors <= radius[1]), EmpiricalCoverage95 = mean(test_errors <= radius[2]))
}))))
# Final radius for the September forecast: the same rule on the 2026 errors only, the most recent realised ones.
# The 2025 errors serve the calibration check above and nothing else
final_radius <- function(kind, group, alpha) error_radius(group_errors(kind, group, "Test 2026"), alpha)

horizon_backtest <- horizon_backtest |>
  left_join(calibration, by = c("Period", "Horizon", "Model")) |>
  arrange(match(Period, c("Validation 2025", "Test 2026")), match(Horizon, c(names(horizon_groups), "30-day mean")),
          match(Model, backtest_models)) |>
  select(Period, Horizon, Model, Paths, N, RMSE, MAE, MeanError, RMSE_gain_vs_Naive, RMSE_gain_vs_SNaive,
         ModelCoverage80, ModelCoverage95, EmpiricalRadius80, EmpiricalRadius95, EmpiricalCoverage80, EmpiricalCoverage95)
kable(select(horizon_backtest, Period:ModelCoverage95), digits = 3,
      caption = "30-day backtest: accuracy against the benchmarks and coverage of the models' own 80% and 95% intervals")
kable(horizon_backtest |> filter(!is.na(EmpiricalCoverage80)) |>
        select(Horizon, Model, N, EmpiricalRadius80, EmpiricalRadius95, EmpiricalCoverage80, EmpiricalCoverage95), digits = 3,
      caption = "Calibration check: empirical intervals with the radius taken from the 2025 backtest errors, coverage on the 2026 paths (radius in SGD/MWh)")

# Check: day 1 of each path against the cached one-step forecast for the same day, which the full run made
# with the same specification on the same re-estimation day
one_step <- rbind(val, test)
day1_check <- bind_rows(lapply(backtest_models, function(kind) {
  path <- backtest[backtest$Model == kind & backtest$Step == 1L, ]
  gap <- abs(path$Prediction - one_step[[kind]][match(path$Date, one_step$Date)])
  data.frame(Model = kind, Paths = length(gap), MaxAbsDifference = max(gap), PathsOver0.01 = sum(gap > 0.01))
}))
kable(day1_check, digits = 3,
      caption = "Day 1 of the backtest paths against the cached one-step forecasts for the same days (SGD/MWh)")
```

```{r month-ahead-text, echo = FALSE}
# Helpers for the numbers quoted in the text below, so that the text always matches the tables
bt <- function(period, kind, group, column) {
  horizon_backtest[[column]][horizon_backtest$Period == period & horizon_backtest$Model == kind & horizon_backtest$Horizon == group]
}
num <- function(x, digits = 1) formatC(x, format = "f", digits = digits)
pct <- function(x, digits = 0) formatC(100 * x, format = "f", digits = digits)
versus <- function(gain) paste(pct(abs(gain)), "%", if (gain >= 0) "lower" else "higher")  # RMSE relative to a benchmark
in_bands <- function(period, kind, column, digits = 1) {  # the three bands, in order
  values <- vapply(names(bands), function(group) bt(period, kind, group, column), numeric(1))
  paste0(num(values[1], digits), ", ", num(values[2], digits), " and ", num(values[3], digits))
}
pct_bands <- function(column) {  # 2026 calibration coverage of SARIMA in the three bands
  values <- vapply(names(bands), function(group) bt("Test 2026", "SARIMA", group, column), numeric(1))
  paste0(pct(values[1]), ", ", pct(values[2]), " and ", pct(values[3]), " %")
}
n_paths <- c(Validation = length(backtest_origins(validation_dates)), Test = length(backtest_origins(test_dates)))
band_rows <- horizon_backtest[horizon_backtest$Model %in% c("SARIMA", "ETS") & horizon_backtest$Horizon %in% names(bands), ]
final_bands <- function(alpha) paste0(num(final_radius("SARIMA", "Days 1-7", alpha)), ", ", num(final_radius("SARIMA", "Days 8-14", alpha)),
                                      " and ", num(final_radius("SARIMA", "Days 15-30", alpha)))
mean_rank <- function(alpha) min(n_paths[["Test"]], ceiling((n_paths[["Test"]] + 1L) * (1 - alpha)))  # rank used for the 30-day average
band_counts <- function(periods) range(vapply(names(bands), function(group) length(group_errors("SARIMA", group, periods)), numeric(1)))
one_step_rmse <- function(column) accuracy_table[[column]][accuracy_table$Model == "SARIMA"]
one_day_radius <- (next_day$Upper80[next_day$Model == "SARIMA"] - next_day$Lower80[next_day$Model == "SARIMA"]) / 2
model_radius_day1 <- as.numeric(september_fc$upper[1, "80%"] - september_fc$lower[1, "80%"]) / 2
```

**Bands, not single days.** The text below reads the three bands and the 30-day average only. Paths start 7 days apart, so within a period a given step always falls on the same weekday: every 2025 path starts on a `r format(validation_dates[1], "%A")` and every 2026 path on a `r format(test_dates[1], "%A")`. A single-step row therefore mixes the horizon with a weekday effect, and it rests on only `r n_paths[["Test"]]` to `r n_paths[["Validation"]]` forecasts. The single-step rows are kept in the table for completeness.

**Accuracy against the benchmarks.** There are `r n_paths[["Validation"]]` paths in 2025 and `r n_paths[["Test"]]` in 2026. The two periods disagree.

- *2025.* SARIMA beats both benchmarks in every band: its RMSE is `r versus(bt("Validation 2025", "SARIMA", "Days 1-7", "RMSE_gain_vs_Naive"))` than Naive's for days 1–7, `r versus(bt("Validation 2025", "SARIMA", "Days 8-14", "RMSE_gain_vs_Naive"))` for days 8–14 and `r versus(bt("Validation 2025", "SARIMA", "Days 15-30", "RMSE_gain_vs_Naive"))` for days 15–30.
- *2026.* SARIMA is level with Naive for days 1–14 and worse than Naive for days 15–30. Its RMSE is `r versus(bt("Test 2026", "SARIMA", "Days 1-7", "RMSE_gain_vs_Naive"))` than Naive's for days 1–7, `r versus(bt("Test 2026", "SARIMA", "Days 8-14", "RMSE_gain_vs_Naive"))` for days 8–14 and `r versus(bt("Test 2026", "SARIMA", "Days 15-30", "RMSE_gain_vs_Naive"))` for days 15–30, where it is also `r versus(bt("Test 2026", "SARIMA", "Days 15-30", "RMSE_gain_vs_SNaive"))` than SeasonalNaive's.
- *Bias in 2026.* SARIMA under-predicts in 2026: its mean error (actual − forecast) in the three bands is `r in_bands("Test 2026", "SARIMA", "MeanError")` SGD/MWh, against `r in_bands("Test 2026", "Naive", "MeanError")` for Naive.
- *30-day average price.* The RMSE of SARIMA's forecast of the 30-day average is `r num(bt("Validation 2025", "SARIMA", "30-day mean", "RMSE"))` in 2025, against `r num(bt("Validation 2025", "Naive", "30-day mean", "RMSE"))` for Naive, and `r num(bt("Test 2026", "SARIMA", "30-day mean", "RMSE"))` in 2026, against `r num(bt("Test 2026", "Naive", "30-day mean", "RMSE"))` for Naive.
- *Growth with the horizon.* From days 1–7 to days 15–30 the RMSE of SARIMA rises from `r num(bt("Validation 2025", "SARIMA", "Days 1-7", "RMSE"))` to `r num(bt("Validation 2025", "SARIMA", "Days 15-30", "RMSE"))` in 2025 and from `r num(bt("Test 2026", "SARIMA", "Days 1-7", "RMSE"))` to `r num(bt("Test 2026", "SARIMA", "Days 15-30", "RMSE"))` in 2026.

So the evidence that a SARIMA path beats the last observed price comes from 2025 only. In 2026, the period closest to September, it does not.

**Main model: SARIMA.** In the 2025 validation backtest SARIMA has a lower RMSE than ETS in all three bands (`r in_bands("Validation 2025", "SARIMA", "RMSE")` against `r in_bands("Validation 2025", "ETS", "RMSE")`), so SARIMA is the main model. This follows the rule used throughout: choose on the validation period, check on the test period. The 2026 backtest gives `r in_bands("Test 2026", "SARIMA", "RMSE")` for SARIMA against `r in_bands("Test 2026", "ETS", "RMSE")` for ETS: it agrees for days 1–7 and 8–14 but not for days 15–30. The choice was made only after the results of both backtests had been seen. It was not fixed in advance, and ETS stays in the backtest table.

**Intervals.**

- *Why by band.* A single step has only `r n_paths[["Validation"]]` (2025) or `r n_paths[["Test"]]` (2026) backtest errors, too few for a 95 % quantile. A band has `r band_counts("Validation 2025")[1]` to `r band_counts("Validation 2025")[2]` errors in 2025 and `r band_counts("Test 2026")[1]` to `r band_counts("Test 2026")[2]` in 2026.
- *Calibration check.* With the radius taken from the 2025 errors, SARIMA's 80 % intervals contain `r pct_bands("EmpiricalCoverage80")` of the 2026 prices in the three bands, and its 95 % intervals `r pct_bands("EmpiricalCoverage95")`. For the 30-day average the figures are `r pct(bt("Test 2026", "SARIMA", "30-day mean", "EmpiricalCoverage80"))` % and `r pct(bt("Test 2026", "SARIMA", "30-day mean", "EmpiricalCoverage95"))` %. Intervals calibrated on 2025 were too narrow for 2026, and more so at longer horizons: SARIMA's absolute errors were larger in 2026 (MAE of `r in_bands("Test 2026", "SARIMA", "MAE")` in the three bands, against `r in_bands("Validation 2025", "SARIMA", "MAE")` in 2025) and biased (see above).
- *Final intervals.* The September intervals use the 2026 backtest errors only, all dated before 31 August 2026. This follows the one-day intervals, which also use the most recent realised errors, and it is a response to the calibration check: intervals built from the 2025 errors did not cover enough in 2026. The 2025 errors are used for that check and nothing else. The radius in the three bands is `r final_bands(0.20)` SGD/MWh for the 80 % interval and `r final_bands(0.05)` for the 95 % interval, against `r in_bands("Test 2026", "SARIMA", "EmpiricalRadius80")` and `r in_bands("Test 2026", "SARIMA", "EmpiricalRadius95")` when taken from the 2025 errors. By construction these intervals contain about 80 % and 95 % of the 2026 errors they are built from, so they cannot be checked on new data.
- *30-day average.* There is one error per path, so the interval of the September average rests on `r n_paths[["Test"]]` errors. The 80 % radius is the error of rank `r mean_rank(0.20)`, `r num(final_radius("SARIMA", "30-day mean", 0.20))` SGD/MWh. The 95 % rank ⌈(n + 1) × 0.95⌉ is `r mean_rank(0.05)`, so the 95 % radius is the largest of the `r n_paths[["Test"]]` errors, `r num(final_radius("SARIMA", "30-day mean", 0.05))` SGD/MWh.
- *Against the one-day interval.* For 1 September the 80 % radius here is `r num(final_radius("SARIMA", "Days 1-7", 0.20))` SGD/MWh, against `r num(one_day_radius)` for SARIMA's one-day interval in Table 15, which is calibrated on the latest 180 one-step errors. The two differ in their calibration sample; for 1 September alone, the interval of Table 15 is the more relevant one.
- *The model's own intervals.* They are shown for comparison and are far too wide: over the three bands and both periods the 80 % intervals of SARIMA and ETS contain `r pct(min(band_rows$ModelCoverage80))` to `r pct(max(band_rows$ModelCoverage80))` % of the actual prices and the 95 % intervals `r pct(min(band_rows$ModelCoverage95))` to `r pct(max(band_rows$ModelCoverage95))` %. They are Gaussian, and their innovation variance is dominated by the high-volatility years 2021–2023 (Table 3): SARIMA's innovation standard deviation is `r num(sqrt(september_fc$model$sigma2))` SGD/MWh, against a one-step RMSE of `r num(one_step_rmse("Val_RMSE"))` in 2025 and `r num(one_step_rmse("RMSE"))` in 2026. For 1 September the model's 80 % radius is `r num(model_radius_day1)` SGD/MWh.

### September path and average price

```{r september-path}
# SARIMA path with the final empirical intervals: radius by band, from the 2026 backtest errors
september_sarima <- path_table(september_fc, "SARIMA", september_dates)
september_path <- data.frame(Date = september_dates, Step = seq_len(horizon), Band = band_of(seq_len(horizon)),
                             SARIMA = september_sarima$Prediction)
for (level in c("80", "95")) {
  alpha <- c("80" = 0.20, "95" = 0.05)[[level]]
  path_radius <- vapply(september_path$Band, function(band) final_radius("SARIMA", band, alpha), numeric(1), USE.NAMES = FALSE)
  september_path[[paste0("Lower", level)]] <- september_path$SARIMA - path_radius
  september_path[[paste0("Upper", level)]] <- september_path$SARIMA + path_radius
}
# the model's own intervals, for comparison only
for (bound in c("Lower80", "Upper80", "Lower95", "Upper95")) september_path[[paste0("Model", bound)]] <- september_sarima[[bound]]
# Naive reference: the price of 31 August carried forward
september_path$Naive <- as.numeric(forecast_30("Naive", price_history$DailyUSEP)$mean)
kable(september_path, digits = 1,
      caption = "September 2026: SARIMA path with empirical 80% and 95% intervals, the model's own intervals for comparison, and the Naive reference (SGD/MWh)")

# September average price: mean of the 30 daily point forecasts; interval from the 2026 backtest errors of the 30-day average
september_mean <- bind_rows(lapply(c("SARIMA", "Naive"), function(kind) {
  point <- mean(september_path[[kind]])
  radius <- c(final_radius(kind, "30-day mean", 0.20), final_radius(kind, "30-day mean", 0.05))
  data.frame(Model = kind, MonthMean = point, Lower80 = point - radius[1], Upper80 = point + radius[1],
             Lower95 = point - radius[2], Upper95 = point + radius[2])
}))
kable(september_mean, digits = 1,
      caption = "September 2026 average price: point forecast with empirical 80% and 95% intervals (SGD/MWh)")
```

```{r fig6, fig.height = 4}
last_month <- daily[daily$Date >= as.Date(format(end_date, "%Y-%m-01")) & daily$Date <= end_date, c("Date", "DailyUSEP")]
xgb_next <- next_prediction[next_prediction$Model == "XGBoost", c("Date", "Prediction")]
path_series <- c("Actual", "SARIMA forecast", "Naive (31 Aug price)")
p6 <- ggplot(september_path, aes(x = Date)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = Lower95, ymax = Upper95, fill = "95%")) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = Lower80, ymax = Upper80, fill = "80%")) +
  geom_line(data = last_month, aes(y = DailyUSEP, colour = "Actual", linetype = "Actual")) +
  geom_line(aes(y = Naive, colour = "Naive (31 Aug price)", linetype = "Naive (31 Aug price)")) +
  geom_line(aes(y = SARIMA, colour = "SARIMA forecast", linetype = "SARIMA forecast")) +
  geom_point(data = xgb_next, aes(y = Prediction, shape = "XGBoost, 1 Sep only"), colour = "white",
             fill = model_colours[["XGBoost"]], size = 2.5, stroke = 0.8) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("80%" = "#596DD5", "95%" = "#D5DBFF")) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = setNames(c("black", "#0000AA", "black"), path_series), breaks = path_series) +
  scale_linetype_manual(values = setNames(c("solid", "solid", "dashed"), path_series), breaks = path_series) +
  scale_shape_manual(values = c("XGBoost, 1 Sep only" = 21)) +
  labs(title = "September 2026: SARIMA 30-day path with empirical intervals",
       subtitle = "Intervals from the 2026 backtest errors by band (days 1-7, 8-14, 15-30). No September actual is used.",
       y = "USEP (SGD/MWh)", fill = "level", colour = "series", linetype = "series", shape = "one-day model")
save_fig(p6, "fig6_september_path.png", 8, 4)
```

**How to read the outlook.** It gives a price level and a range of uncertainty, not a direction. In the 2026 backtest SARIMA is level with Naive for days 1–14 and worse than Naive for days 15–30, so the path is not evidence that prices will move away from the 31 August price. The SARIMA forecast of the September average is `r num(september_mean$MonthMean[september_mean$Model == "SARIMA"])` SGD/MWh and the Naive one `r num(september_mean$MonthMean[september_mean$Model == "Naive"])`; the gap between them, `r num(abs(diff(september_mean$MonthMean)))`, is `r if (abs(diff(september_mean$MonthMean)) < final_radius("SARIMA", "30-day mean", 0.20)) "smaller" else "larger"` than the 80 % radius of the SARIMA average, `r num(final_radius("SARIMA", "30-day mean", 0.20))`.

**Limitations.**

- *Bias.* In the 2026 backtest SARIMA under-predicts systematically, and more so at longer steps: its mean error (actual − forecast) is `r in_bands("Test 2026", "SARIMA", "MeanError")` SGD/MWh in the three bands. The intervals are symmetric around the point forecast and do not correct for this.
- *Intervals from past errors.* The intervals are built from the errors of one period, 2026, with one radius per band. They describe the errors seen in that period and cannot anticipate an abrupt change in the price level. They cannot be checked on new data, and for the 30-day average they rest on `r n_paths[["Test"]]` errors.
- *Small backtest.* `r n_paths[["Validation"]]` and `r n_paths[["Test"]]` paths, started 7 days apart and 30 days long, overlap heavily, so their errors are strongly dependent and count for far fewer independent observations. Each period is a single year (2026 only to August), and the two give different answers.
- *Model choice after the fact.* SARIMA was made the main model after both backtests had been seen.
- *Price history only.* The path uses no information on September demand, fuel prices, reserve prices or weather, and the SARIMA specification was selected by `auto.arima()` on one-step fit, not on 30-day accuracy.
- *Numerical reproducibility.* Both models are estimated by numerical optimisation. Day 1 of each backtest path repeats a cached one-step forecast of the full run, with the same specification, data and re-estimation day. In this document the two differ by at most `r num(day1_check$MaxAbsDifference[day1_check$Model == "SARIMA"], 2)` SGD/MWh for SARIMA and `r num(day1_check$MaxAbsDifference[day1_check$Model == "ETS"], 2)` for ETS, where `r day1_check$PathsOver0.01[day1_check$Model == "ETS"]` of `r day1_check$Paths[day1_check$Model == "ETS"]` paths differ by more than 0.01. The full run and this knit can be on different machines, whose daily means differ in their last floating-point digits, and the ETS estimates are sensitive to that. The ETS rows of the backtest should therefore be read to the nearest unit, not to the decimals shown; SARIMA is far less affected.

# Export

```{r export}
# Feature tables actually used for each test week (one preprocessing cut-off per re-estimation)
collect_test_features <- function(i) {
  cutoff <- test_dates[i] - 1L
  dat <- prepare_features(cutoff, min(end_date, cutoff + refit_days))
  dat <- dat[dat$Date > cutoff, ]
  dat$PreprocessingCutoff <- cutoff
  dat
}
processed_test <- bind_rows(lapply(seq(1L, length(test_dates), by = refit_days), collect_test_features))

write_xlsx(list(Daily = usep_sample, Train_Features = initial_data, Test_Features = processed_test,
                Temperature_CV = temperature_cv, Holiday_Dates = data.frame(Date = holiday_dates)),
           file.path(output_dir, "processed_data.xlsx"))

write_xlsx(list(Descriptive = annual, Stationarity = stationarity, Frozen_Settings = frozen_table,
                Accuracy = accuracy_table, Residuals_InSample = insample_tests, Residuals_Errors = error_diagnostics,
                DM_vs_Naive = as_table(dm9), DM_Top3 = as_table(dm10), DM_Holm = as_table(p_holm),
                DM_HAC = dm_hac, Candidates = candidate_table,
                Regime = regime, Bias_Top3 = bias_table, Concentration = concentration,
                DM_External = as_table(dm11), Incremental = incremental_scores,
                Ancillary_Check = ancillary_check,
                Ancillary_Variants = ancillary_table, Ancillary_DM = ancillary_dm, Intervals = interval_summary,
                TPC = tpc_log, Spike_Normal = spike_table, NextDay = next_day, Intervals_Daily = intervals,
                Sept_Path = september_path, Sept_Mean = september_mean, Horizon_Backtest = horizon_backtest),
           file.path(output_dir, "report_tables.xlsx"))
```

# Appendix: temperature reconstruction

```{r appendix-temperature}
longest_gap <- function(x) {
  r <- rle(is.na(x))
  max(c(0L, r$lengths[r$values]))
}
temp_gaps <- data.frame(Station     = stations,
                        MissingDays = colSums(is.na(usep_sample[stations])),
                        LongestGap  = vapply(usep_sample[stations], longest_gap, numeric(1)),
                        Lambda      = c(NA, temperature_lambda[stations[-1]]))
kable(temp_gaps, row.names = FALSE, caption = "Missing station-days, 2021-01-01 to 2026-08-31")
c(DaysWithoutRawFiveStationMean = sum(is.na(usep_sample$TempSG_raw)))

# Reconstruction error at the chosen lambda (N counts masked evaluations, not distinct days)
kable(temperature_cv[temperature_cv$Lambda == temperature_lambda[temperature_cv$Station], ], digits = 3,
      row.names = FALSE, caption = "Table B1. Station reconstruction error at the chosen lambda")
```
